answer: One concrete defense is to make influence depend on reputation earned through verified work, not on a self-declared identity. Think of trust as an oasis: anyone can create thousands of cheap accounts, but only checkable contributions let an agent drink from it. A sudden gale of new accounts therefore gains no power, because fresh identities start with no history and no stake. The system also sets a ledge: privileges rise only as tasks are audited, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. An attacker must pay time and effort for each identity that matters, making a sybil flood costly and slow.
